text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Membership of the EMU currency union is no obstacle to active economic stimulation measures in Sweden, National Debt Office chief Thomas Franzen says.
- The Swedish trades union organisation LO demands that the government retract new unemployment benefit rules due to take effect at the turn of the year.

- The Hell's Angels bikers' gang refuses to leave its club headquarters in central Malmo despite a police eviction order. The clubhouse was severely damaged in a recent bomb attack thought to be the work of the rival Bandidos gang.
- The use of special winter tyres, which can be studded or made from special high-friction rubber, is likely to become obligatory next year.
- The information technology is crying out for skilled labour, and could employ up to 6,000 people straight away -- this despite total unemployment of 12.8 percent in Sweden.
- Carl-Johan Bonnier, president of the Bonnier group which owns Dagens Industri, denies a report in the Swedish media that its BAF unit -- which owns Dagens Industri -- is to seek a market listing.
- Statements from the Riksbank governor and deputy governor on Wednesday caused chaos on the debt market on Thursday.
Some dealers bought Swedish bonds on the assumption that the Riksbank would cut key rates on Thursday only to take heavy losses when the bank made no such move.
- ABB chief executive office Percy Barnevik is to step down in favour of Goran Lindahl, thereby halving his working hours to 40 to 50 per week. Barnevik will remain ABB board chairman.
